nodes.description: ATG7 activates ATG12 before its conjugation to ATG5, which promotes expansion of the preautophagosomal phagophore, and it facilitates lipidation of LC3-I with phosphatidylethanolamine to generate LC3-II. LC3-II sits on the inner and outer autophagosomal membranes and recruits cytoplasmic cargo directly or through selective adaptor proteins. Without ATG7 both conjugation systems fail, so the phagophore cannot expand and cargo cannot be marked for capture.

nodes.description: Patient cells show impaired autophagic flux and markedly reduced autophagic sequestration. Importantly this is a severe reduction, not a complete abolition: evidence of basal autophagy was readily identified in patient fibroblasts and skeletal muscle despite loss of ATG7. nodes.description: p62 (SQSTM1) is the classical autophagy cargo receptor: it recruits cytoplasmic cargo to autophagosomes through interaction with LC3-II and is itself degraded after autolysosome formation. When LC3-II cannot be generated, p62 is neither consumed nor able to deliver cargo, and it accumulates. This is the cardinal cellular readout that failed lipidation has actually blocked cargo degradation, and it is the practical diagnostic biomarker alongside the LC3-II immunoblot.
